title: Choirs

lines: ONE CHORD NONE COULD MAKE ALONE.
cards: Four people stand in a row, each singing a different note. Alone, the low note sounds gloomy. The high one sounds thin.
The two in the middle sound like they've lost the tune. Then they sing at the same moment, and the four odd notes become one chord, full and warm, that none of them could make alone.

That's the whole secret of a choir: a cathedral choir in white robes, a gospel choir swaying on the beat, an Orthodox choir singing a service from start to finish, six faithful people in a village church.

teach.h: AS ONE, TO MAKE ONE SOUND.
teach.b: Start at the temple. When Solomon's temple is dedicated, Chronicles says: "It came even to pass, as the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD."
Then, the story says, the house was filled with a cloud. The singing comes first; the glory follows.

Next, one mouth, many voices. Paul writes to the Christians in Rome: "That ye may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ." One mouth sounds like everyone saying the same thing.
But in a choir, sopranos, altos, tenors and basses each sing a different line, and the unity is in the harmony, not in sameness. If everyone sang the melody, you'd lose the chord.
Then, a choir on a wall. In Nehemiah, Jerusalem's broken walls have been rebuilt, and Nehemiah sets two great companies of singers giving thanks on top of the wall.
They go opposite ways and meet at the house of God: two choirs, singing a city back to life.

Last, near the Bible's end, John hears heaven in Revelation: "And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth."
Countless voices, each its own, poured into one sound. In this scene, heaven doesn't whisper. It sings.

how: Church choirs come in different forms: robed cathedral and parish choirs, gospel choirs, Orthodox choirs that sing the whole liturgy, and small groups of volunteers who rehearse during the week and lead the congregation's singing on Sunday.

o: the clergy who chant the prayers at the altar
the soloists hired to sing alone at weddings
groups singing different parts as one sound

p: as one, to make one sound

s: in a choir, unity means everyone sings the same note
sopranos, altos, tenors and basses each sing a different line. the unity is in the harmony.
at the temple, the singers were 'as one, to make one sound'
and Chronicles says the house was then filled with a cloud.
in Revelation 19, John hears heaven as one lone voice
he hears "the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters," saying Alleluia.

games.q: you're Nehemiah. Jerusalem's walls are rebuilt, and it's time to give thanks. how do you arrange the singers?
o: one big crowd at the main gate.
two great companies, walking the wall in opposite directions.
a single singer on the highest tower.
games.why: two companies giving thanks set off in opposite directions along the wall and met at the house of God.

practice: If someone's with you, hum a tune you both know, a hymn or a lullaby, and listen for the moment your voices meet.
If you're alone, hum one part along with a choir recording, the low line or the high one, and notice how it fits inside the whole.
If you pray, you can let the song be your prayer alongside other voices; if you don't, listen for the place where many voices become one sound.

wordCard.voice: Choirs. Many voices, each holding its own part, making one sound to praise God.

carryVoice: Your line: many voices. Each one holds its own part, and the chord needs all of them. See you next time.
